newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil BNDES expects CVRD mines assessment soon.
newsitem.headline: Brazil BNDES expects CVRD mines assessment soon.

text.p: An independent assessment of gold and copper finds by state mining firm Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) in northern Brazil is expected to be ready soon, a National Development Bank (BNDES) spokeswoman said.

She said the report by analysts Mineral Research Development Inc (MRDI) should be ready in time to be discussed at the next meeting of Brazil's National Privatization Council (CND), tentatively scheduled for February 6.

The government is awaiting the report assessing CVRD's recent discovery of promising gold and copper deposits in the Carajas region of Para state to finalize the rules for CVRD's selloff scheduled for April.

CVRD announced the discovery of a possible large gold deposit at Igarape-Bahia in the Carajas area in October last year but says it is still too early to say exactly how much gold there is and whether it is viable to mine.
The company has declined to comment on a geological report cited in O Estado de Sao Paulo newspaper today as confirming huge new gold and copper deposits in Carajas.
CVRD market relations officer Marcos Antonio Pinto said the company did not want to comment on the contents of the geological report because it would involve revealing an internal document.
He retracted an earlier statement saying the report had not been commissioned by CVRD and its contents were herefore not known to the company.
He said CVRD had indeed asked Canadian geologist Robert Mason to carry out the evaluation in October shortly after the Igarape-Bahia find.
Pinto said it would be another three months, however, before CVRD could say with relative certainty how large the deposit really was.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
